chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Aban ibn Taghlub who said:
I was praying behind Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at al-Muzdalifa. When he finished, he turned toward me and said: 'O Aban!

The five obligatory prayers — whoever upholds their limits and preserves their prescribed times will meet God on the Day of Resurrection, and for him will be a covenant with Him by which He will admit him into Paradise.
And whoever does not uphold their limits and does not preserve their prescribed times will meet God with no covenant for him — if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him.'

key_terms.الصَّلَوَاتُ الْخَمْسُ الْمَفْرُوضَاتُ: The five obligatory prayers (salat) — the foundational pillar of Islamic worship
key_terms.حُدُودَهُنَّ: Their limits/conditions — the jurisprudential requirements of proper prayer performance
key_terms.عَهْدٌ: A covenant/pledge — a divine binding promise, here God's guarantee of Paradise for the faithful prayer-keeper
key_terms.مَوَاقِيتِهِنَّ: Their prescribed times — the specific time windows for each of the five daily prayers

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the five obligatory prayers and their prescribed times?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addressed his companion Aban ibn Taghlub after a congregational prayer at al-Muzdalifa during the Hajj pilgrimage. The Imam taught that whoever fulfills the five daily obligatory prayers with all their conditions and within their prescribed times carries a divine covenant guaranteeing entry into Paradise, while those who neglect these prayers are left entirely to God's discretion — facing either punishment or forgiveness with no assured guarantee.
